chunks.label: Yes, I did it
chunks.rationale: Cheer when you succeed or get lucky.
chunks.interference: yatta is your own win; yatta ne cheers someone else's.

chunks.label: It's fine, no problem
chunks.rationale: Reassure people that all is well.
chunks.interference: nan demo nai (it's nothing) vs nan demo ii (anything is fine).

chunks.label: Oh right, so true
chunks.rationale: Agree, confirm, or show you just remembered something.
chunks.interference: a, sou da is remembering, not agreeing.

chunks.label: What is that
chunks.rationale: React when something surprises you or catches your eye.
chunks.interference: nani kore is about things near you, nani sore near the other person.

chunks.label: Really, no way
chunks.rationale: Show disbelief at surprising news.
chunks.interference: uso desho doesn't call anyone a liar.

chunks.label: Oh no, what now
chunks.rationale: React when something goes wrong.
chunks.interference: shimatta is about your mistake; dou shiyou is not knowing what to do next.

chunks.label: Oh and whoa sounds
chunks.rationale: Make the quick noises that show surprise.
chunks.interference: ara is mild surprise; arara is 'oh dear' at a mishap.

chunks.label: Hmm and huh sounds
chunks.rationale: Show you're listening, or that you're not impressed.
chunks.interference: Drawn out, fuun, hai hai and haa can all sound rude.

chunks.label: Praising someone
chunks.rationale: Cheer someone else's success or good luck.
chunks.interference: yoku yatta talks down, so not to a boss.

chunks.label: Looks good
chunks.rationale: Approve of how something looks or is going.
chunks.interference: It's yosasou, not ii sou.

chunks.label: Congratulations
chunks.rationale: Congratulate birthdays, weddings, exams and graduations.
chunks.interference: Polite forms add go- to kekkon and sotsugyou, but not to goukaku.

chunks.label: That sounds hard
chunks.rationale: Show sympathy when someone has had a rough time.
chunks.interference: taihen is hassle and effort; tsurai is emotional pain.

chunks.label: Take it easy, get well
chunks.rationale: Show care for someone who is rushed or unwell.
chunks.interference: None.
members: 風邪ひかないようにね

chunks.label: Forget it, whatever
chunks.rationale: Drop a topic or brush something off.
chunks.interference: dou demo ii (I don't care) vs nan demo ii (anything is fine).

chunks.label: No no, come on
chunks.rationale: Deny or laugh off praise, ideas and claims.
chunks.interference: iya iya is modest; sore wa nai is a firm no.

chunks.label: Effort and ta-da sounds
chunks.rationale: Fill the moments of lifting, counting in and showing off.
chunks.interference: None.

chunks.label: Ouch and damn it
chunks.rationale: React to pain, defeat and feeling foolish.
chunks.interference: chikushou is rough; yarareta works for anyone.

chunks.label: Told you so
chunks.rationale: Point out you were right, or call out a hypocrite.
chunks.interference: yoku iu here is sarcastic, not 'people often say'.
members: だから言ったじゃない

chunks.label: Hey, stop it
chunks.rationale: Get attention, protest, or hush someone.
chunks.interference: oi is rough; use sumimasen to get a stranger's attention.

chunks.label: Year-end and New Year
chunks.rationale: Greet people around Christmas and New Year.
chunks.interference: yoi otoshi o is before January 1, akemashite omedetou after.
members: あけましておめでとう
今年もよろしくお願いします
今年もお世話になりました

chunks.label: Leave me alone
chunks.rationale: Recognize the angry outbursts you'll hear in films and fights.
chunks.interference: All are rough except hottoite, the only one safe to say yourself.

drops.reason: Tokenizer fragment of どうでもいい, which is kept.
Duplicate of 何でもない (same phrase written in kana).
Duplicate of もういい with sentence-final yo.
